questions.q: In Five year plans, Plan Holiday is from .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1966-1969. Key Points

• Plan Holiday:-

• It​ was a break in the Five Year Plans of India, during which no new plan was launched.

• It was from 1966 to 1969 when the third plan ended and the fourth plan began.

• The break was taken to evaluate the progress of the previous plans and to make necessary changes in the upcoming plan.

• The decision to take a Plan Holiday was made by the then Prime Minister of India, Indira Gandhi.

• The Plan Holiday helped in improving the economy and reducing poverty in India.

Additional Information

• Five-Year Plans:-

• It refer to the country's series of comprehensive economic development strategies.

• The planning process was initiated by the Planning Commission (and later replaced by NITI Aayog).

• Each plan outlined the government's priorities, sectoral allocations, and development goals for a five-year period.

• The concept of five-year plans was popularized by the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin's leadership. The Soviets used these plans to rapidly industrialize and develop the economy.

questions.q: In February 2022, the Delhi High Court reserved judgement on a series of Public Interest Litigations (PILs) challenging which exception in Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Marital rape. Key Points

• The PILs challenge the exception clause in Section 375 which excludes marital rape from the definition of rape.

• The challenge is significant as it could lead to the criminalization of marital rape and provide more protection to women against sexual violence within marriage.

• Physical torture, dowry death, and suicide are not exceptions in Section 375, but they are related to crimes against women in India.

• Physical torture and dowry death are often associated with domestic violence and dowry-related crimes, respectively.

• Suicide is not a crime, but it is often linked to mental health issues and social pressures faced by women in India.

Additional Information

• Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code deals with the offence of rape.

• The exception being challenged in the PILs is the exception clause which states that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under fifteen years of age, is not rape.

• Marital rape refers to any unwanted sexual acts by a spouse or ex-spouse that is committed without the other person's consent.

• Physical torture refers to any act of violence that causes physical harm or injury to a person.

• Dowry death refers to the murder or suicide of a woman who is unable to meet the demands of her husband or his family for a dowry.
